_comment: Gaps where AI is the object of the gap rather than the instrument that would move it. Default is ai-as-instrument; only exceptions are listed. See methodology/taxonomy.md section 2b.

frames.name: AI Could Be Misused
frames.rationale: Asks which AI capability would move a gap about AI misuse. The dimension presupposes AI is the instrument acting on a science problem; here AI is the subject matter, and the two independent labelers split between Coordination and institutional and LLM reasoning precisely because neither is a real answer.

frames.name: AI Could Go Rogue
frames.rationale: Tier 3 here means the field cannot agree what evidence would establish an AI system is safe. That is a different phenomenon from quantum gravity's tier 3, where physicists disagree about what would settle a question about nature, so its tier is not comparable to the rest of the map.

frames.name: AI is Still Narrow in its Reasoning and Planning
frames.rationale: The gap is the AI capability itself, so 'which AI capability would move it' is circular and its maturity label means something different from every other row: the capability and the gap are the same object.

frames.name: Labor-Replacing AI Could Lead to Human Disempowerment
frames.rationale: Found by a blind relabeler applying the criterion rather than the enumeration, and it meets the test cleanly: the gap does not exist if AI does not. Its tier-3 measurability is contested for the same reason as the other ai-as-object gaps — we are arguing about a technology we are building — so it is not comparable to the natural-science tier-3 cases.
